description:
Programme or Project Overview

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) recruits five CREATE PhD Programme Fellows, a Wellcome-funded global health doctoral training programme with studies beginning in September 2027. CREATE trains researchers to address major global health challenges through interdisciplinary research spanning epidemiology, infectious disease, immunology, health economics and health policy, with research projects designed jointly with partners in LMIC settings and a structured programme of training, fieldwork and secondment.

Fellowships are fully funded: the award covers tuition fees, a tax-free stipend at the standard UKRI rate, research and fieldwork costs, and travel connected to the programme. Fellows join LSHTM - one of the world's top institutions for public and global health research - and benefit from its supervision capacity across infectious-disease epidemiology, clinical trials, statistics and policy research. The cohort structure provides peer support, mentoring and cohort-wide training throughout the four years.

Candidate profile and application

Applicants hold, or expect to complete, a master's degree or equivalent research experience in public health, epidemiology, medicine, statistics, laboratory science or a related field relevant to global health. Applications are submitted through LSHTM's recruitment portal (reference ITD-CRD-2026-24) with a CV, transcripts, references and statements addressing the programme's selection criteria; the closing date is 8 November 2026.

Highlights

  • 5 Wellcome-funded CREATE PhD Programme Fellowships
  • Interdisciplinary global health research training
  • Fees, stipend, research and fieldwork costs covered
  • LMIC-partnered projects and secondments
  • September 2027 start at LSHTM London
  • Closing date: 8 November 2026

About London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM)

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is a world-leading research university for public and global health, consistently ranked at the top of its field internationally. Its research spans epidemiology, infectious disease, immunology, health economics and health policy, with major multi-country trial and training programmes funded by Wellcome, UKRI and the global health agencies. LSHTM runs structured, fully funded doctoral training programmes such as CREATE for global health research, and recruits fellows and research staff through its online recruitment portal.
